question: Which Article of the Indian Constitution abolishes 'Untouchability' and forbids its practice in any form?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Article 17.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Article 17 of the Constitution abolishes 'Untouchability' and forbids its practice in any form; enforcing any disability arising out of untouchability is a punishable offence in accordance with law. (अस्पृश्यता का अंत — अनुच्छेद 17)

 

• Article 17 falls under Part III (Fundamental Rights), within the group of rights called the Right against Exploitation (Articles 17-18, along with Articles 23-24).

 

• Parliament gave effect to Article 17 through the Untouchability (Offences) Act, 1955, later renamed and made more stringent as the Protection of Civil Rights Act, 1976.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The other Rights against Exploitation are Article 23 (prohibition of traffic in human beings and forced labour/begar) and Article 24 (prohibition of employment of children below 14 years in factories, mines or other hazardous occupations).

 

NOTE

 

• Article 15 (Option 1): Prohibits discrimination on grounds of religion, race, caste, sex or place of birth.

 

• Article 16 (Option 2): Guarantees equality of opportunity in matters of public employment.

 

• Article 18 (Option 4): Abolishes titles, except military and academic distinctions.

question: Which of the following is the largest brackish water (saltwater) lagoon in India, located in the state of Odisha?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Chilika Lake.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Chilika Lake is the largest coastal lagoon in India and the second largest in the world (after the New Caledonian lagoon), lying along the Bay of Bengal coast across Puri, Khordha and Ganjam districts of Odisha. (चिल्का झील — ओडिशा)

 

• It was designated a Ramsar Site (Wetland of International Importance) in 1981, the first site in India to receive this status.

 

• The lake is famous as a habitat for the Irrawaddy dolphin and for hosting large numbers of migratory birds at the Nalabana Bird Sanctuary within it.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Vembanad Lake (Kerala) is India's largest freshwater lake, part of the Kerala backwaters.

 

• Sambhar Lake (Rajasthan) is India's largest inland saline/salt lake, a major source of salt production.

 

NOTE

 

• Vembanad Lake (Option 1): Freshwater, not brackish; located in Kerala.

 

• Pulicat Lake (Option 3): India's second-largest brackish water lagoon, on the Andhra Pradesh-Tamil Nadu border.

 

• Sambhar Lake (Option 4): An inland saline lake, not a coastal lagoon; located in Rajasthan.

question: When did Linus Carl Pauling receive the Nobel Prize in Chemistry for ‘his research into the nature of the chemical bond and its applications to the elucidation of the structure of complex substances’?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1954.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Linus Carl Pauling was awarded the Nobel Prize in Chemistry in 1954 for his research into the nature of the chemical bond and its application to the elucidation of the structure of complex substances. (लिनुस पॉलिंग — रसायन विज्ञान नोबेल पुरस्कार 1954)

 

• Pauling's work laid the foundation of modern structural chemistry and molecular biology, including concepts like electronegativity, resonance, and hybridization.

 

• He is one of only four people to have won two unshared Nobel Prizes; he later won the Nobel Peace Prize in 1962 for his campaign against above-ground nuclear weapons testing.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Nobel Prize in Chemistry has been awarded by the Royal Swedish Academy of Sciences since 1901.

 

NOTE

 

• 1950 (Option 2): The Chemistry Nobel that year went to Otto Diels and Kurt Alder for the discovery and development of the diene synthesis (Diels-Alder reaction).

 

• 1956 (Option 3): The Chemistry Nobel that year went to Cyril Norman Hinshelwood and Nikolay Semyonov for research on the mechanism of chemical reactions.

 

• 1958 (Option 4): The Chemistry Nobel that year went to Frederick Sanger for work on the structure of proteins, especially insulin.

question: Daskathia of _________ is the tribal dance performed by two males depicting the historic and Puranic events.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Odisha.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Daskathia is a traditional ballad/dance form of Odisha, performed by two male performers who narrate historic and Puranic events while holding wooden clappers called kathi. (दासकठिया — ओडिशा)

 

• The name comes from 'Kathi' (wooden clappers) that the performers, known as Gayakas, clap together to keep rhythm while narrating stories, often devoted to Goddess Ramachandi.

 

• It is a folk art combining storytelling, music, and dramatic gestures, traditionally performed in rural Odisha.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Other folk dance/art forms of Odisha include Pala, Ghoomura, Chhau (Mayurbhanj), and Danda Nata.

 

NOTE

 

• Uttar Pradesh (Option 1): Known for folk forms like Raslila and Nautanki, not Daskathia.

 

• Gujarat (Option 2): Known for Garba and Dandiya Raas, not Daskathia.

 

• Goa (Option 3): Known for Dekhni and Fugdi, not Daskathia.

question: KA Najeeb Vs Union of India case deals with violation of rights under____________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Article 21.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• In Union of India vs K.A. Najeeb (2021), the Supreme Court held that prolonged incarceration without trial violates the fundamental right to a speedy trial guaranteed under Article 21 of the Constitution, and this can override the strict bail restrictions of the UAPA. (के.ए. नजीब मामला — अनुच्छेद 21)

 

• The Court ruled that statutory restrictions on bail (such as under Section 43D(5) of the Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act) do not oust the constitutional courts' power to grant bail on grounds of violation of Article 21 when there has been an inordinate delay in trial.

 

• This judgment reinforced that the right to life and personal liberty under Article 21 includes the right to a speedy trial.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Article 21 states: 'No person shall be deprived of his life or personal liberty except according to procedure established by law.'

 

• The right to speedy trial was earlier recognised as part of Article 21 in Hussainara Khatoon vs State of Bihar (1979).

 

NOTE

 

• Article 16 (Option 1): Deals with equality of opportunity in matters of public employment.

 

• Article 14 (Option 3): Guarantees equality before law and equal protection of laws.

 

• Article 19 (Option 4): Guarantees six fundamental freedoms such as speech, expression, assembly, etc.

question: Which of the following is the red algae?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Rhodophyceae.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Rhodophyceae, commonly known as red algae, are mostly marine and owe their red colour to the pigment r-phycoerythrin, which masks other pigments like chlorophyll. (रोडोफाइसी — लाल शैवाल)

 

• Common examples include Polysiphonia and Porphyra; some are used commercially to obtain agar and carrageenan.

 

• Red algae store food as floridean starch and their cell walls often contain calcium carbonate.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Algae are classified largely by their pigmentation: Chlorophyceae (green), Phaeophyceae (brown), and Rhodophyceae (red).

 

NOTE

 

• Chlorophyceae (Option 2): Known as green algae; the dominant pigments are chlorophyll a and b, giving them a grass-green colour.

 

• Liverwort (Option 3): A bryophyte, not an algal group.

 

• Phaeophyceae (Option 4): Known as brown algae; the brown colour comes from the pigment fucoxanthin.

question: What will be the atomic number of an element X which is placed in period 2 and group 17?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 9.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• An element placed in Period 2 and Group 17 of the modern periodic table is Fluorine (F), whose atomic number is 9. (फ्लोरीन — परमाणु क्रमांक 9)

 

• Its electronic configuration is 2, 7 (1s² 2s² 2p⁵), meaning the second shell has 7 electrons, matching Group 17 (halogens, needing one more electron for a stable octet).

 

• Group 17 elements are called halogens (F, Cl, Br, I, At); Fluorine is the most electronegative and reactive element in the periodic table.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Period 2 elements range from Lithium (3) to Neon (10).

 

• Fluorine is used in toothpaste (as fluoride) and in the manufacture of Teflon.

 

NOTE

 

• 8 (Option 1): Atomic number of Oxygen, which lies in Group 16, Period 2.

 

• 7 (Option 2): Atomic number of Nitrogen, which lies in Group 15, Period 2.

 

• 10 (Option 3): Atomic number of Neon, which lies in Group 18, Period 2.

question: In which two consecutive years was there no chief guest at the Republic Day celebrations of India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 2021 and 2022.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• India had no foreign chief guest at the Republic Day parades of 2021 and 2022, the only two consecutive years this has happened since independence. (गणतंत्र दिवस — 2021 और 2022 में कोई मुख्य अतिथि नहीं)

 

• In 2021, UK Prime Minister Boris Johnson was invited but cancelled his visit due to the surging COVID-19 situation in the UK.

 

• In 2022, Brazilian President Jair Bolsonaro was invited but could not attend, reportedly due to the model code of conduct in force for state elections and rescheduling issues linked to the pandemic.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• The tradition of inviting a foreign head of state/government as chief guest to the Republic Day parade began in 1950 with Indonesian President Sukarno.

 

• In 2023, Egyptian President Abdel Fattah el-Sisi was the chief guest.

 

NOTE

 

• 2019 and 2020 (Option 2): Chief guests were Cyril Ramaphosa (South Africa, 2019) and Jair Bolsonaro (Brazil, 2020).

 

• 2020 and 2021 (Option 3): 2020 had a chief guest (Bolsonaro); only 2021 had none, so this pairing is incorrect.

 

• 2018 and 2019 (Option 4): 2018 had ASEAN leaders (10 heads of state/government) as chief guests, and 2019 had Cyril Ramaphosa.

question: Fisher’s quantity theory is explained by his famous equation given as ________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is MV = PT.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Irving Fisher's Quantity Theory of Money is expressed through the equation of exchange: MV = PT. (फिशर का विनिमय समीकरण — MV = PT)

 

• Here, M = quantity/stock of money in circulation, V = velocity of circulation of money, P = general price level, and T = total volume of transactions (goods and services traded).

 

• The equation implies that the total money spent (MV) in an economy equals the total value of goods and services transacted (PT), and that the price level varies directly with the quantity of money, other factors remaining constant.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Fisher's theory is a foundational concept in classical monetary economics, later refined by economists like the Cambridge economists (Marshall, Pigou) into the cash-balance approach.

 

NOTE

 

• MP = VT (Option 1), MT = PV (Option 3), PV = MV (Option 4): These are not valid forms of Fisher's equation of exchange; only MV = PT correctly relates money supply, velocity, price level and transactions.

question: Before the rise of the modern industrial system, Indian exports consisted chiefly of manufactures like________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is cotton and silk fabrics.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Before the rise of the modern industrial system, India was well known worldwide for its handicraft industries, and its exports consisted chiefly of finished manufactured goods such as cotton and silk fabrics. (सूती और रेशमी वस्त्र — प्रमुख निर्यात)

 

• India also exported items like calicoes, muslin, and other high-quality fabrics, along with artisanal products, and was regarded as an exporter of finished goods rather than raw materials.

 

• After British colonial rule and industrialisation in Britain, this pattern reversed — India became an exporter of raw materials (like raw cotton, indigo) and importer of finished manufactured goods, notably machine-made textiles from Britain.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• This is a classic theme in NCERT Class 8 History (Our Pasts III), describing India's transition from an exporter of manufactured goods to an exporter of raw materials during colonial rule.

 

NOTE

 

• Electricals (Option 1), Chemicals (Option 2), Light machinery (Option 3): These are modern/industrial-era manufactured goods, not part of pre-industrial India's traditional export basket, which was dominated by textiles.

question: The Kanchenjunga peak is located in which sub-division of Himalaya from the following?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Darjeeling and Sikkim Himalayas.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Kanchenjunga peak, the third-highest mountain in the world, is located in the Darjeeling and Sikkim Himalayas, a sub-division of the Himalayas lying between the Tista and Dihang river systems. (कंचनजंगा शिखर — दार्जिलिंग व सिक्किम हिमालय)

 

• This division lies between the Singalila range in the west and the Chumbi Valley in the east, and includes the state of Sikkim and the Darjeeling hills of West Bengal.

 

• The Himalayas are broadly divided (west to east) into Kashmir/Punjab Himalayas, Himachal-Uttaranchal (Kumaon) Himalayas, Darjeeling-Sikkim Himalayas, and Arunachal Himalayas.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Kanchenjunga (8,586 m) lies on the India-Nepal border and is the highest peak entirely within India.

 

NOTE

 

• Kashmir Himalayas (Option 1): Lie between the Indus and Sutlej rivers, including ranges like Karakoram, Ladakh, Zaskar, and Pir Panjal.

 

• Himachal and Uttaranchal Himalayas (Option 3): Lie between the Sutlej and Kali rivers, covering Himachal Pradesh and Uttarakhand.

 

• Arunachal Himalayas (Option 4): Lie between the Bhareli/Kameng and Diphu rivers, extending eastward from the Bhutan border to the Diphu Pass.

question: Guru Bipin Singh, a Nrityacharya awardee, Sangeet Natak Akademi awardee and Kalidas Samman awardee, was renowned for promoting which classical dance form?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Manipuri.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Guru Bipin Singh was a renowned exponent and guru of Manipuri dance, credited with popularising and systematising the classical form beyond Manipur. (गुरु बिपिन सिंह — मणिपुरी नृत्य)

 

• He received the Sangeet Natak Akademi Award, the Kalidas Samman, and is honoured with the title 'Nrityacharya' for his contribution to Manipuri dance.

 

• He founded institutions like the Manipuri Nartanalaya to train dancers in this classical form, which is characterised by graceful, fluid movements depicting themes from Radha-Krishna Raslila.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Manipuri is one of the eight classical dance forms of India recognised by the Sangeet Natak Akademi.

 

NOTE

 

• Kuchipudi (Option 2): Classical dance of Andhra Pradesh.

 

• Odissi (Option 3): Classical dance of Odisha.

 

• Kathak (Option 4): Classical dance form associated with North India.

question: Who holds the authority of transferring judges from one High court to another High Court?
option_1: The senior most judge of Supreme Court
solution_text:
The correct answer is The President of India.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Under Article 222 of the Constitution, the President of India has the authority to transfer a judge from one High Court to another, after consultation with the Chief Justice of India. (न्यायाधीशों का स्थानांतरण — राष्ट्रपति की शक्ति)

 

• The recommendation for such a transfer is initiated and processed through the Collegium system, but the formal transfer order is issued by the President.

 

• This power is meant to maintain the independence and uniformity of the higher judiciary across states.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Article 217 deals with the appointment of High Court judges; Article 222 specifically deals with their transfer.

 

NOTE

 

• The senior most judge of Supreme Court (Option 1): Has no independent constitutional authority to transfer judges.

 

• The Chief Justice of India (Option 2): Is consulted in the process and effectively initiates recommendations via the Collegium, but does not hold the formal transferring authority — that rests with the President.

 

• The Law Minister of India (Option 4): Has no constitutional power to transfer judges.

question: ___________ is the process of complete or incomplete oxidation or hydrolysis of fats and oils when exposed to air, light, moisture, or bacterial action that spoils food.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Rancidification.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Rancidification is the process of complete or incomplete oxidation or hydrolysis of fats and oils when exposed to air, light, moisture, or bacterial action, which spoils food by producing unpleasant smell and taste. (विकृतगंधिता — वसा और तेल का खराब होना)

 

• It commonly affects foods with high fat content, such as butter, ghee, and fried snacks, upon prolonged storage.

 

• Antioxidants (like BHA, BHT, and Vitamin E) are added to fatty foods to delay rancidification and extend shelf life.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Rancidity can be of two types: oxidative rancidity (due to oxidation of fat by atmospheric oxygen) and hydrolytic rancidity (due to hydrolysis of fat by moisture/enzymes).

 

NOTE

 

• Hydrogenation (Option 2): The process of adding hydrogen to unsaturated fats to convert them into saturated fats (e.g., making vegetable oil into vanaspati).

 

• Auto-oxidation (Option 3): A specific chemical mechanism (spontaneous reaction with atmospheric oxygen) that can contribute to rancidity, but the overall spoilage process described here is termed rancidification.

 

• Auto reduction (Option 4): Not a recognised term for fat/oil spoilage; it does not describe this process.

question: Which of the following is a Tibeto-Burmese language?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Tripuri.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Tripuri (Kokborok), spoken mainly in Tripura, belongs to the Tibeto-Burman branch of the Sino-Tibetan language family. (त्रिपुरी/कोकबोरोक — तिब्बती-बर्मी भाषा परिवार)

 

• The Tibeto-Burman languages are spoken predominantly in the northeastern Himalayan and hill regions of India, including languages like Bodo, Garo, Mizo, and Manipuri.

 

• India's languages broadly fall into four families: Indo-Aryan, Dravidian, Austroasiatic, and Sino-Tibetan (Tibeto-Burman).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Kokborok was declared an official language of Tripura, alongside Bengali and English.

 

NOTE

 

• Odia (Option 1) and Assamese (Option 3): Belong to the Indo-Aryan language family.

 

• Tulu (Option 4): Belongs to the Dravidian language family.

question: Who among the following was the author of the play ‘Mrichchhakatika’?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Shudraka.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Mrichchhakatika ('The Little Clay Cart') is a Sanskrit play written by Shudraka, depicting the love story of the impoverished Brahmin merchant Charudatta and the courtesan Vasantasena. (मृच्छकटिकम् — शूद्रक)

 

• It is notable for portraying social realism, blending romance with political intrigue, unlike most classical Sanskrit dramas that focus on royal or mythological themes.

 

• Very little is known about Shudraka himself; he is traditionally described as a king-poet in the prologue of the play.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Other important Sanskrit playwrights include Kalidasa (Abhijnanasakuntalam), Bhasa (Swapnavasavadattam), and Vishakhadatta (Mudrarakshasa).

 

NOTE

 

• Kalidasa (Option 1): Author of Abhijnanasakuntalam, Malavikagnimitram, and Vikramorvasiyam, not Mrichchhakatika.

 

• Amarasimha (Option 2): Author of the Sanskrit lexicon Amarakosha, not a playwright.

 

• Bhasa (Option 4): Author of plays such as Swapnavasavadattam and Pratijnayaugandharayana, not Mrichchhakatika.

question: Select the FALSE statement from the given options.
option_1: Baikal rocks are formed from the dissolved materials that precipitate from the solution.
option_2: The sedimentary rocks are formed by the deposition and subsequent cementation of that material within bodies of water and at the surface of the earth.
option_3: Metamorphic rocks may be formed simply by being deep beneath the Earth’s surface, subjected to high temperatures and the great pressure of the rock layers above it.
option_4: Igneous rock is formed through the cooling and solidification of magma or lava.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Baikal rocks are formed from the dissolved materials that precipitate from the solution.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• This statement is FALSE. There is no standard rock classification termed 'Baikal rocks' that forms from precipitation of dissolved materials; that description actually applies to certain chemical sedimentary rocks (e.g., rock salt, gypsum, some limestones). (चट्टानें — भ्रामक कथन 'बैकाल रॉक्स')

 

• Statement 2 is correct: Sedimentary rocks are formed by the deposition and subsequent cementation of material within bodies of water and at the earth's surface.

 

• Statement 3 is correct: Metamorphic rocks form when existing rocks are subjected to high temperature and pressure deep beneath the Earth's surface, without melting.

 

• Statement 4 is correct: Igneous rocks form through the cooling and solidification of magma (below the surface) or lava (above the surface).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Rocks are broadly classified into three types: Igneous, Sedimentary, and Metamorphic, together forming the basis of the rock cycle.

 

• Sedimentary rocks are further divided into clastic, chemical (formed from precipitation), and organic/biogenic sedimentary rocks.

 

NOTE

 

• Options 2, 3 and 4 are correct, factual descriptions of sedimentary, metamorphic, and igneous rocks respectively, and hence are not the answer to this 'select the FALSE statement' question.

question: Pathans in North-West India organised the society of Khudai Khidmatgars, popularly known as Red Shirt, under whose leadership?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Khan Abdul Ghaffar Khan.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Khudai Khidmatgars ('Servants of God'), popularly known as the Red Shirts, was a non-violent movement organised among the Pathans (Pashtuns) of North-West India under the leadership of Khan Abdul Ghaffar Khan. (खुदाई खिदमतगार — खान अब्दुल गफ्फार खान)

 

• Khan Abdul Ghaffar Khan, popularly known as 'Frontier Gandhi', founded the movement in 1929 in the North-West Frontier Province, advocating non-violence inspired by Mahatma Gandhi.

 

• The Khudai Khidmatgars actively participated in the Civil Disobedience Movement and later merged their political efforts with the Indian National Congress.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Khan Abdul Ghaffar Khan was awarded India's highest civilian honour, the Bharat Ratna, in 1987 — the first non-Indian citizen to receive it.

 

NOTE

 

• Muhammad Ali (Option 1): One of the Ali Brothers, associated with the Khilafat Movement, not the Khudai Khidmatgars.

 

• MA Ansari (Option 2): A prominent Congress leader and physician, not associated with founding the Khudai Khidmatgars.

 

• Hasrat Mohani (Option 4): A poet and freedom fighter known for coining the slogan 'Inquilab Zindabad', not associated with the Khudai Khidmatgars.

question: In which of the following States/Union Territories were the 36th National Games held?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Gujarat.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The 36th National Games were held in Gujarat from 29 September to 12 October 2022, across multiple host cities including Ahmedabad, Surat, Vadodara, Rajkot, Gandhinagar, and Bhavnagar. (36वें राष्ट्रीय खेल — गुजरात)

 

• These Games were originally scheduled earlier but were postponed multiple times due to the COVID-19 pandemic before finally being held in Gujarat.

 

• The Games' mascot was 'Sawaj' (Asiatic Lion cub), and Gujarat topped the medal tally at these Games.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The 37th National Games were held in Goa in 2023.

 

NOTE

 

• Rajasthan (Option 1), New Delhi (Option 2), Kerala (Option 4): None of these hosted the 36th National Games.

question: Which of the following was established in Bombay in 1875?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Arya Samaj.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Arya Samaj was founded by Swami Dayanand Saraswati in Bombay in 1875, as a reformist Hindu movement based on the infallibility of the Vedas. (आर्य समाज — स्वामी दयानंद सरस्वती, 1875, बंबई)

 

• Its motto was 'Krinvanto Vishwaram Aryam' ('Make this world noble'), and it opposed idol worship, child marriage, and the caste system while promoting Vedic education and social reform.

 

• Dayanand Saraswati's book 'Satyarth Prakash' laid out the core philosophy of the Arya Samaj.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Arya Samaj later established the Dayanand Anglo-Vedic (DAV) chain of schools and colleges to promote modern education alongside Vedic values.

 

NOTE

 

• Satyashodhak Samaj (Option 1): Founded by Jyotirao Phule in Pune in 1873.

 

• Aligarh movement (Option 2): Led by Sir Syed Ahmed Khan, centred on the founding of the Muhammadan Anglo-Oriental College at Aligarh in 1875, not in Bombay.

 

• Brahmo Samaj (Option 3): Founded by Raja Ram Mohan Roy in Calcutta in 1828.

question: Which of the following options conveys the meaning of the word ‘Republic’ in the Indian Constitution?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Elected head.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The term 'Republic' in the Indian Constitution signifies that the head of the state (the President) is elected, either directly or indirectly, and does not hold office by heredity. (गणराज्य — निर्वाचित प्रमुख)

 

• India's President is elected indirectly by an Electoral College comprising elected members of Parliament and state legislative assemblies, for a term of five years.

 

• This is in contrast to a monarchy, where the head of state holds power through hereditary succession.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Preamble of the Indian Constitution describes India as a 'Sovereign, Socialist, Secular, Democratic Republic'.

 

NOTE

 

• Nominated head (Option 2), Subordinate head (Option 3), Hereditary head (Option 4): None of these describe the meaning of 'Republic'; a hereditary head, in fact, describes a monarchy, the opposite of a republic.

question: Who among the following was defeated in the battle of Chanderi in 1528?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Medini Rai.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Battle of Chanderi (1528) was fought between Babur and the Rajput ruler Medini Rai, the governor of Chanderi (Malwa region), who was defeated and killed in this battle. (चंदेरी का युद्ध 1528 — मेदिनी राय पराजित)

 

• This battle followed Babur's decisive victory over Rana Sanga at the Battle of Khanwa (1527), and was part of Babur's consolidation of power in central India.

 

• After the battle, Chanderi fort came under Mughal control.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Babur founded the Mughal Empire in India after his victory at the First Battle of Panipat (1526) against Ibrahim Lodi.

 

NOTE

 

• Shershah Suri (Option 1): Founder of the Sur Empire; he defeated Humayun (Babur's son), and was not involved in the Battle of Chanderi.

 

• Babur (Option 2): The victor, not the one defeated, in the Battle of Chanderi.

 

• Sikandar Lodi (Option 3): A Delhi Sultanate ruler of the Lodi dynasty, who ruled before Babur's invasion and was not involved in the Battle of Chanderi.

question: The venue of the 2020 Olympic Games was _________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Tokyo.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The 2020 Olympic Games were held in Tokyo, Japan; although officially retaining the name 'Tokyo 2020', the Games were actually held from 23 July to 8 August 2021, postponed by a year due to the COVID-19 pandemic. (टोक्यो 2020 ओलंपिक — जापान)

 

• This marked the second time Tokyo hosted the Summer Olympics, the first being in 1964.

 

• India won a total of 7 medals at the Tokyo Olympics — its best-ever performance at the time — including a gold in javelin throw by Neeraj Chopra.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The next Summer Olympics, Paris 2024, were held in France.

 

NOTE

 

• Sydney (Option 1): Hosted the 2000 Summer Olympics.

 

• Rio (Option 2): Hosted the 2016 Summer Olympics (Rio de Janeiro, Brazil).

 

• Los Angeles (Option 4): Hosted the 1932 and 1984 Summer Olympics, and is scheduled to host the 2028 Summer Olympics.

question: When was the International Day of the Girl Child 2021 celebrated?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 11 October.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The International Day of the Girl Child is observed every year on 11 October, including in 2021, to highlight and address the needs and challenges girls face while promoting their empowerment. (अंतर्राष्ट्रीय बालिका दिवस — 11 अक्टूबर)

 

• The day was established by the United Nations General Assembly in December 2011, with the first observance in 2012.

 

• The theme for the 2021 observance was 'Digital generation. Our generation.'

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• India also observes a National Girl Child Day on 24 January every year.

 

NOTE

 

• 14 October (Option 1), 12 October (Option 2), 13 October (Option 3): None of these are the correct date; the International Day of the Girl Child is fixed on 11 October every year.

question: In January 2022, which State Government has extended its integrated initiative for the empowerment of persons with disabilities (PwDs) — the Bhima Bhoi Bhinnakhyama Samarthya Abhiyan (BBSA) – for the next five years?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Odisha.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• In January 2022, the Odisha Government extended its integrated initiative for the empowerment of persons with disabilities (PwDs), the Bhima Bhoi Bhinnakhyama Samarthya Abhiyan (BBSA), for the next five years. (भीम भोई भिन्नक्षम समर्थ्य अभियान — ओडिशा)

 

• The scheme is named after the blind poet-saint Bhima Bhoi and aims to provide financial assistance, aids, appliances, and support services to persons with disabilities in Odisha.

 

• It was launched under the Odisha government's Social Security and Empowerment of Persons with Disabilities (SSEPD) Department.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Other Odisha welfare schemes include Madhu Babu Pension Yojana and Biju Swasthya Kalyan Yojana (BSKY).

 

NOTE

 

• Manipur (Option 2), Jharkhand (Option 3), West Bengal (Option 4): None of these states run the BBSA scheme; it is specific to Odisha.
